title: Customer usage quirks, feature buckets, and priority heatmap
content:
TL;DR:
Quick roll-up of recurring product usage quirks we observed in interviews + support logs (Mar-May 2026). Grouped requests into pragmatic feature buckets and plotted a crude priority heatmap (impact x effort). This doc focuses on low-effort patches we can prototype in a single sprint and a small experiment slate to validate a couple of mid-effort asks.

Background / data sources:
- 28 customer interviews (CS-run, sample skewed to mid-market + 6 enterprise trials).
- Support ticket crawl (last 90 days): 412 tickets with tags: latency, routing, model-mismatch, embedding-ops.
- Two product analytics queries (console usage, route variants): see CONFLUENCE-12345 for SQL notes.
- Quick dev notes from runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412

Observed "quirks" (concrete, repeatable behaviors):
1) Implicitly pinned models: many teams assume the API will preserve their previous model even if they specify just model_family in route config; surprise when minor changes roll through. Typical quote: "We thought the same model would stick — then generation drifted."
2) Token-cost surprise on streamed responses: streaming + structured output reduces debuggability of token counts in console; customers reported unexpected bill spikes after enabling streaming.
3) Embedding drift across quantized variants: teams using dedicated pools reported small L2 shifts when switching quantized variants; caused reranking differences that are hard to debug.
4) Canaries get starved during bursts: canary traffic weight logic + autoscaling sometimes routes all burst traffic to primary pool for speed reasons; canaries see near-zero traffic when load spikes.
5) Confusing error surfaces for tool-calling failures: stack traces are opaque — engineers often open a ticket with logs attached asking which component (router, runtime, model) raised the error.
6) Re-entrancy on cached prefixes not obvious: customers assume cache refresh semantics are synchronous; in reality prefix cache invalidation is eventual which causes stale outputs for a short window.

Feature buckets (grouped from asks + inferred fixes):
- A: Model-stability controls (pin-by-version, explicit model-lock, rollout visualization)
- B: Billing transparency for streaming (token previews, per-chunk estimates)
- C: Embedding diff tooling (L2 comparator, explainable rerank score deltas)
- D: Canary resilience (traffic hedging, burst-aware weighting)
- E: Error triage surface (structured error codes across stack, suggested owner tag)
- F: Cache semantics clarity (cache-ttl dashboard, sync-invalidate API)

Priority heatmap (rough, from customer-impact x dev-effort heuristics):
- Quick wins (High impact, Low effort): B, E, F
  - Example low-effort tasks: add token-estimate flag to streaming API (server-side calc + console hint), map common error codes to owner labels and return structured payloads, add a "cache ttl" column to route settings and a manual invalidate button in the console.
- Mid runway (High impact, Medium effort): A, D
  - Model-lock visuals + explicit pinned-version API (needs backend + console change). Canary hedging needs routing policy work in router layer and some autoscaler hooks.
- Longer-term (Medium impact, High effort): C
  - Embedding diffs + explainability requires a small analytics pipeline plus UI to surface rerank deltas for customers.

Low-effort patch list (candidate sprint items):
1) streaming-token-preview (JIRA-REW-7812) — server calculates token-estimate for first N chunks and surface in console before enabling streaming. Dev estimate: 3 dev-days + 1 QA.
2) structured-error-contract — map 12 most common runtime errors to a structured schema that includes suggested owner: {router|runtime|model|customer}. Dev estimate: 2 dev-days, cross-ref with SRE.
3) cache-ttl-console-column + invalidate button — expose TTL and add manual invalidate that triggers immediate prefix eviction. Dev estimate: 4 dev-days.
4) quick-doc blurb + SDK sample for 'pinning' semantics — make expectations explicit in docs and SDK. Docs/SDK: 2 days.

Experiment slate (to validate mid-effort asks):
- Canary hedging A/B: enable hedging for 10% of customers (randomized route) and measure canary exposure during bursts for 30 days. Metrics: canary traffic share, rollout failure detection latency, error rate. Instrumentation owner: platform-engineering.
- Pin-by-version opt-in pilot: recruit 4 customers to test explicit model-lock API; observe drift complaints and rollback frequency. Product/solutions owner: Marta V.

Quick customer-facing notes (what to tell customers now):
- Be explicit about model_version in route config if you need bit-for-bit stability. We're adding 'pin' wording to console copy this week.
- Streaming may show token-count variance; use the new token-preview toggle when available to estimate cost.
- If you see small embedding rerank differences after switching quantization, open a support ticket with sample vectors and model/variant ids (we can provide a diff tool while we build the UI).

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How strongly do we want to enforce 'pin' semantics vs. encourage pinned versions by UX only? (i.e., API-level immutability could complicate rollouts).
- Should canary hedging be on by default for Dedicated customers, or opt-in? (Default hedging improves safety but adds routing complexity and cost).
- For embedding diffs, what privacy constraints apply when we surface customer vectors in tooling? Need legal check.

Next steps / owners:
- Kick off mini-sprint for Quick wins (B, E, F): owner: Benji Ortega — roadmap sync 2026-05-20.
- Design doc for Model-lock UX and API: owner: Connor Li — draft due 2026-06-02. Link to PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412
- Legal consult on embedding tooling: owner: Marta Venkatesh — EOD 2026-05-25.

Notes to self / meeting checklist for sync with eng (use this agenda):
1) Walk through quick-win tickets and assign dev owners (15m)
2) Show example support tickets demonstrating the error triage pain (10m)
3) Discuss canary hedging experiment gating criteria (10m)
4) Decide on docs blurb wording and release timing (5m)

Slack threads / useful links:
- #cs-product-feedback (pinned message 2026-05-11)
- CONFLUENCE-12345 (dataset queries + support ticket export)
- JIRA-REW-7812 (streaming token-preview epic)

----
Rough raw snippets pulled from interviews (verbatim where noted):
- "We had a spike and the canary disappeared — it looked like our canary just never existed. That was scary." (enterprise payments team)
- "I toggled streaming to see if responses would be faster. Next month’s bill was 2x. No idea which prompt caused it." (marketplace search startup)
- "Pinning should be a first-class thing — we don't want to be surprised by model tweaks when we're on payroll codepaths." (HR SaaS infra lead)

If any of you want to split ownership on quick-wins or take the experimental leads, comment here or add yourself to CONFLUENCE-12345 > Owners table.

-- Aisha K.
